_note: Week of June 8–14, 2026. Indian. Monday is non-fish (tandoori chicken) — standing rule. Fish midweek (Wed shrimp coconut curry, Thu cod masala) + shrimp in Tue wraps. Raita is the standalone sauce card (Indian cousin of tzatziki). Tikka Tuesday = paneer + leftover shrimp naan wraps. Sunday breakfast-for-dinner = masala egg bhurji + besan chilla (Indian, not waffles). Chicken OK at dinner in moderation — only Mon for Laine; her lunches stay non-chicken. Onion only cooked (no raw); no mushrooms/okra/eggplant; no lentils (chana uses chickpeas). Mild for Laine, Jake adds chili to his portion. Paneer (homemade — stores don't carry it) for calcium; cauliflower + peas for cruciferous + fiber.

tzatziki.name: Mint Cucumber Raita
tzatziki.note: Jake's tzatziki, gone to India. Cool yogurt sauce that tames every curry and makes the naan wraps. Nonfat Greek yogurt keeps the fat negligible. Makes ~1.5 cups, keeps 4–5 days. Mild — leave the green chili out for Laine, add a pinch to your own bowl, Jake.

ingredients.item: English cucumber — ½ large, grated and squeezed dry
Ground cumin — ½ tsp (toasted if you can)
Dried mint — 1 tsp (or 2 tbsp fresh, chopped)
Green chili — Jake's bowl only, finely minced (skip for Laine)

steps: Grate cucumber on the large holes of a box grater. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible in a towel — this keeps the raita thick.
Stir together yogurt, squeezed cucumber, lemon juice, cumin, mint, cilantro, and salt.
Taste and adjust — more cumin, more salt, more lemon. It should be cool and herby.
Chill at least 30 min before serving so the flavors meld.
Keep Laine's portion mild; Jake stirs a little minced green chili into his own bowl. Keeps 4–5 days covered.

dinners.name: Tandoori Chicken + Basmati + Cumin Cauliflower
dinners.note: Non-fish opener — chicken marinated in spiced yogurt (the tandoori trick, no grill needed), roasted with cauliflower for a cruciferous hit, basmati underneath. Chicken's fine for Laine at dinner; this is the only chicken on her plate all week. Jake adds chili to his.

ingredients.item: Cauliflower — Jake 200g, Laine 170g, cut into florets
Greek yogurt (plain nonfat) — 4 tbsp shared (tandoori marinade)
Garam masala, turmeric, cumin, paprika, ginger, salt
Lemon juice + fresh cilantro to finish

steps: Mix yogurt with garam masala, turmeric, cumin, paprika, ginger, salt, and a squeeze of lemon. Coat the chicken and let it sit 30 min if you can (longer is better).
Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss cauliflower with olive oil, cumin, salt on a sheet pan.
Roast cauliflower 10 min, then add the marinated chicken to the same pan. Roast 18–22 min more until chicken hits 165°F and the edges char.
Cook basmati: rinse until clear, simmer in 1.5× water 12 min, rest 5 min, fluff.
Slice chicken, plate over rice with cauliflower. Cilantro + lemon to finish. Jake gets more chicken and adds chili.

dinners.name: Paneer & Shrimp Tikka Naan Wraps with Raita
dinners.note: This week's leftovers-plus-a-treat night. Our stores don't carry paneer, so we make it at home (foolproof — milk + lemon); make the full batch now and save some for Saturday's palak paneer. Last week's shrimp gets a tikka rub, the homemade paneer is the treat protein — both seared hot and tucked into warm homemade garlic naan with cool raita, cucumber, and tomato. Jake loads both proteins and adds chili to his; Laine goes shrimp-forward and mild.

ingredients.item: Homemade paneer — Jake 90g, Laine 60g, cubed (from whole milk + lemon; see method)
Homemade garlic naan — Jake 2, Laine 1 (see the Homemade Garlic Naan recipe → Sides)
Raita — 3–4 tbsp per wrap (see recipe card)
Cherry tomatoes — ½ cup shared, halved
Garam masala, paprika, cumin, salt — green chili for Jake

steps: Make the garlic naan ahead — see the Homemade Garlic Naan recipe (Sides tab). Start its dough first so it can rest while you make the paneer.
Make the paneer: bring 1 gallon whole milk to a gentle boil in a big pot, stirring now and then so it does not scorch.

Kill the heat and stir in 3–4 tbsp lemon juice (or white vinegar), a splash at a time, until the milk curdles — white curds separating from greenish, clear-ish whey (~30 sec). If it has not fully split, add a little more acid.
Pour through a cheesecloth-lined colander. Rinse the curds under cool water to wash off the tang, then gather the cloth and squeeze out the excess whey.
Wrap the curds tight in the cloth and press under a heavy pot or a couple of cans for 20–30 min until firm, then cube. Makes ~450–500g — set aside ~215g for Saturday. Keeps 4–5 days covered.
Make the raita ahead if you can (see recipe) — better after 30 min in the fridge.
Toss shrimp and the remaining paneer (separately) with olive oil, garam masala, paprika, cumin, salt.
Sear paneer in a hot pan 1–2 min per side until golden; set aside. In the same pan, cook shrimp 2 min per side until just pink.
Build wraps: smear of raita on a warm naan, then shrimp + paneer, cucumber, tomato. Jake loads both proteins and adds minced green chili; Laine goes shrimp-forward and mild.

dinners.name: Shrimp Coconut Curry + Basmati + Spinach
dinners.note: A mild, creamy coconut curry — light coconut milk keeps the fat in check. Onion is fully cooked into the base (no raw), spinach wilted in at the end for iron. Jake stirs chili into his bowl.

ingredients.item: Yellow onion — ½ cup shared, finely diced (cooked down)
Garam masala, turmeric, cumin, ginger, salt — chili for Jake

steps: Cook basmati (rinse, simmer in 1.5× water 12 min, rest, fluff).
Sauté onion in olive oil over medium until soft and golden, 5–6 min. Add garam masala, turmeric, cumin, ginger — bloom 30 sec.
Add diced tomatoes, simmer 5 min until jammy. Stir in coconut milk, warm through.
Add shrimp, simmer gently 3–4 min until just cooked. Don't boil hard or the coconut splits.
Wilt in spinach off the heat. Serve over basmati. Jake's bowl gets chili; Laine's stays mild.

dinners.name: Baked Cod Masala + Basmati + Peas
dinners.note: Easiest night of the week. Cod baked in a jarred tikka masala sauce, peas stirred in for fiber and color, basmati underneath. Mild and weeknight-fast.

ingredients.item: Tikka masala simmer sauce — ~¾ cup shared

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Pat cod dry, place in a baking dish.
Spoon tikka masala sauce over the cod to coat. Scatter peas around.
Bake 16–18 min until cod flakes and the sauce bubbles.
Meanwhile cook basmati.
Plate rice, cod, sauce, and peas. Finish with cilantro and a squeeze of lemon. Jake gets the bigger piece and extra sauce.

dinners.name: Chana Masala + Cauliflower + Basmati
dinners.note: Vegetarian fiber night — chickpeas, not lentils. A proper chana masala with a cooked onion-tomato base, plus roasted cauliflower on the side. Big fiber, plant-forward, satisfying.

ingredients.item: Garbanzo beans — Jake 0.7 can, Laine ~0.45 can
Yellow onion — ½ cup shared, finely diced (cooked down)
Garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, ginger, salt — chili for Jake

steps: Roast cauliflower at 425°F with a little oil, cumin, and salt, ~20 min.
Sauté onion in olive oil until golden, 6–7 min. Add garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, ginger — bloom 30 sec.
Add diced tomatoes, simmer 5 min. Add drained chickpeas + a splash of water, simmer 10 min, lightly mashing some for body.
Cook basmati.
Serve chana over rice with cauliflower alongside. Jake adds chili; Laine stays mild. Cilantro and lemon to finish.

dinners.name: Palak Paneer + Basmati
dinners.note: Calcium + iron night for Laine: paneer in a silky spinach gravy. Use the homemade paneer you made on Tuesday (or make a fresh batch — same method). Onion cooked all the way down, mild and creamy. Jake gets more paneer and a little chili.

ingredients.item: Homemade paneer — Jake 130g, Laine 85g, cubed (Tuesday's batch, or make fresh — see Tuesday)
Baby spinach — ~220g shared (it cooks way down)
Yellow onion — ½ cup shared, finely diced (cooked down)
Garam masala, cumin, ginger, garlic, salt — chili for Jake

steps: Use the paneer you made Tuesday (or make a fresh batch: boil 1 gallon whole milk, curdle with 3–4 tbsp lemon juice, strain through cheesecloth, rinse, and press 20–30 min until firm; cube).
Lightly sear the paneer cubes in a little oil until golden; set aside.
Sauté onion until soft, add cumin, garam masala, ginger, garlic — bloom 30 sec.
Add spinach in batches until wilted, then blend the mixture smooth (immersion blender). Loosen with a splash of water.
Return to low heat, fold the paneer back in, warm 3–4 min. Keep it mild for Laine.
Serve over basmati. Jake gets more paneer and stirs chili into his.

dinners.name: Masala Egg Bhurji + Besan Chilla
dinners.note: Standing breakfast-for-dinner, Indian edition. Egg bhurji is spiced Indian scrambled eggs; besan chilla are savory chickpea-flour pancakes (the 'pancake' of the night) — high protein, naturally gluten-free, mild. Cool raita on the side. Jake gets the bigger portion and chili; Laine stays mild. Onion cooked, not raw.

ingredients.item: Liquid egg whites — Jake ½ cup, Laine ¼ cup
Yellow onion — ½ cup shared, finely diced (cooked into the bhurji)
Turmeric, cumin, garam masala, salt — chili for Jake
Raita on the side (see recipe card)

steps: Chilla batter: whisk besan with water to a thin pancake batter, plus a pinch of turmeric, cumin, and salt. Let it sit while you start the bhurji.
Bhurji: sauté onion in a little oil until soft, add turmeric, cumin, garam masala, then the tomatoes; cook 3–4 min.
Beat eggs + egg whites, pour in, and scramble gently until just set. Keep Laine's mild; Jake stirs chili into his.
Chilla: ladle batter into a hot oiled nonstick pan, spread thin, cook 2 min per side until golden. Make Jake's bigger.
Serve bhurji with the chilla and a scoop of raita. Cilantro on top.

jakeLunch.name: Chicken Tikka & Chickpea Bowl
jakeLunch.note: Indian batch bowl, same 5-container Sunday format, no fish (office-friendly). Yogurt-marinated chicken tikka, chickpeas, cumin-roasted cauliflower, basmati, with a raita drizzle. Add the raita fresh when eating so it stays cool. Heads-up: basmati pushes carbs up this week. You can swap it for cauliflower rice using the dropdown — if you do, drop the roasted cauliflower florets from your batch so you're not doing double-cauliflower.

ingredients.item: Chicken breast — ~2.3 lbs total (210g raw per container)
Garbanzo beans — 2 cans total (0.4 can per container)

substitutions.item: Cauliflower rice (cooked) — same volume, ~1 cup per container

ingredients.item: Greek yogurt (plain nonfat) — ~3 tbsp per container (tikka marinade + drizzle)
Garam masala, turmeric, cumin, paprika, ginger, garlic, salt

steps: Marinate all chicken in yogurt + garam masala, turmeric, cumin, paprika, ginger, garlic, salt — 30 min if you have it.
Roast chicken at 425°F ~22–24 min until cooked through. Rest, then dice.
Roast cauliflower with oil, cumin, salt, ~20 min.
Warm chickpeas in a pan with a little oil and spice 5 min.
Cook all basmati at once.
Divide into 5 containers: rice, chicken, chickpeas, cauliflower. Add raita fresh when eating, not batched.

laineLunch.name: Curried Tuna & Chickpea Pasta Jar — Mason Jar Style
laineLunch.note: Indian-spin on the cold jar. Curry-yogurt dressing kept separate, chickpeas and peas for fiber, bell pepper and cucumber for crunch. No chicken, no lentils, eaten cold over two sittings.
laineLunch.dressingNote: Curry-yogurt: 3 tbsp nonfat Greek yogurt + ½ tsp curry powder + squeeze of lemon, in a separate container per jar.

ingredients.item: Canned tuna in water — 1 can per jar (5 cans total)
Garofalo pasta (rotini or penne) — 225g dry total, 45g per jar
Frozen peas — ~¼ cup per jar, thawed
Baby spinach — big handful per jar (~30g)
Greek yogurt (plain nonfat) — ~3 tbsp per jar (curry dressing, separate)

steps: Cook pasta in salted water, drain, rinse cold, toss with a tiny bit of olive oil.
Thaw peas. Dice bell pepper, slice cucumber, drain tuna well, rinse chickpeas.
Layer each jar: pasta → chickpeas → tuna → peas → bell pepper + cucumber → spinach on top.
Mix the curry-yogurt dressing; portion into a small separate container per jar.
To eat: pour in dressing, shake, eat half — reseal for the second sitting.

laineBreakfasts.name: Greek Yogurt Parfait
steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl. Top with thawed berries and flaxseed.

laineBreakfasts.name: Masala Egg White Scramble
laineBreakfasts.note: Mild masala scramble — just a pinch of turmeric and cumin, no heat.
steps: Sauté bell pepper 2 min with a pinch of turmeric and cumin.
Add egg whites, scramble over medium-low until just set.
Toss in spinach at the end. Top with cheese.

laineBreakfasts.name: Birch Benders Waffles + Berries
laineBreakfasts.note: Waffles, not pancakes. Same batter, crisp edges.

ingredients.item: Birch Benders pancake/waffle mix — ½ cup dry

steps: Mix batter: mix + egg whites + water per package. Stir in flaxseed.
Cook in a preheated waffle iron 3–4 min until crisp.
Top with thawed berries.

laineSnacks.desc: ½ cucumber sliced + 4 tbsp raita for dipping. Cool and mild.

extras.name: Homemade Garlic Naan
extras.note: Soft, blistered garlic naan on the stovetop — no tandoor needed. Batch makes ~6. Great with any of the curries this week; we use it for Tuesday's wraps and the extras go with Wednesday's coconut curry. With yeast it's pillowy; the quick baking-powder version is weeknight-fast.

ingredients.item: Butter or ghee — 4 tbsp total (2 in dough, 2 for garlic butter)
Instant yeast — 1 tsp (or 1 tsp baking powder + ¼ tsp baking soda for a quick version)
Warm water or milk — ⅓ cup

steps: If using yeast: bloom 1 tsp yeast + 1 tsp sugar in ⅓ cup warm water for 5 min until foamy. (Quick version: skip the yeast and use 1 tsp baking powder + ¼ tsp baking soda instead.)
Mix 2 cups (250g) flour with ¾ tsp salt (and the baking powder/soda if using the quick version).
Stir in ½ cup yogurt, 2 tbsp melted butter, and the yeast water. Knead into a soft, slightly tacky dough ~5 min.
Cover and rest: ~1 hr with yeast (until puffy), or 15 min for the quick version.
Divide into 6 balls. Roll each into an oval about ¼-inch thick.

Heat a cast-iron skillet over high. Lay a naan down, cook 1–2 min until big bubbles form, then flip and cook ~1 min more until charred spots appear. (Brush the top with a little water before flipping for extra puff.)
Keep cooked naan warm under a towel while you do the rest.
Garlic butter: melt 2 tbsp butter with the minced garlic. Brush over the hot naan and finish with chopped cilantro.
Best fresh, but they reheat well wrapped in foil in a warm oven, or 15 sec in the microwave under a damp towel.
